capability.script_layout: 5 parameters (boostback delay, iip aim, throttle, pitch, yaw); no entry-burn vector; ignitions = boostback + landing

reasoning: The booster aero is an attitude-independent Cd(M) table ('grid fins stowed' blunt-cylinder configuration) flown through a point-mass propagator with drag along -v: the unpowered phase has ZERO lift/flap/bank authority, so the only entry-deceleration lever is how the boostback cutoff state is placed.

The graded 100 t landing reserve plus the predicted landing need pin the corridor mass to >= ~400 t; at that ballistic coefficient (Cd ~ 1.1-1.3 above Mach 1, A = 63.617 m2) the terminal velocity near 3 km is ~330-490 m/s and a ballistic arrival overshoots it -- probes arrive at 1053-1150 m/s for every 5-parameter script tried.

The 250 kPa planning cap cannot be honoured by diving earlier: q exceeds 250 kPa at ~10 km while the vehicle still travels ~1100 m/s, and no shallower unpowered trim exists without lift -- probes peak at 439-809 kPa.
The closed-loop landing forecast (4.0 g law, h0 = 3 km) grades the arrival infeasible: predicted touchdown 745-833 m/s against the 3/1 m/s limits, i.e. CORRIDOR_MISSED.

Even the lightest state legal under the reserve gate (dry + 100 t reserve) arrives above the closed-loop landing envelope, so a lighter derived variant does not close it either; the E5-07 gap (restart-2 aerodynamic entry) is a MODELLED-AERO capability gap, not a planner representation gap -- the representation now exists and the flight verdict is honest.
Guidance is the secondary category: with lift/bank steering the unpowered phase could trade the 12 g / 250 kPa budget across a long skip glide; the model provides no such control to plan.

probes.note: all on the sealed separation states; closed-loop need model, 250 kPa / 12 g graded, reserve 'target' + 2.5 t margin; search=keep single-eval unless noted; dt_opt 0.5 s, dt_final 0.25 s

dc7_differential_evolution_box.conclusion: the global search maps the whole boostback-placement box and never finds a feasible unpowered entry: the whole box misses the closed-loop corridor

rows.note: the unpowered profile keeps +172.6 t in the tanks that the 1-burn entry burn would spend

rows.metric: corridor propellant margin over need+100 t reserve+2.5 t recipe, t

rows.note: corridor v_max 350 m/s; the closed-loop need model rejects the unpowered arrival
two-burn landing never ignites: the corridor verdict rejects the handover

comparison_vs_sealed_three_burn_dc7.summary: the two-burn profile saves ~173 t of entry propellant and ~193 t of reserve margin, but the modelled aero cannot trade that mass for a corridor-legal arrival: with no lift authority the saved propellant stays as ballast (heavier vehicle, faster arrival, higher q), and the corridor is missed. The three-burn design pays the entry burn precisely to decelerate above the q-limited atmosphere.
